title: Bishop and knight: Delétang
summary: Mating with bishop and knight: the barrier drives the black king to the edge, Delétang's triangles take it to the corner of the bishop's colour, and the final net delivers mate before the fifty-move rule.
history:
King, bishop and knight against a lone king looks like an easy ending, but few players know how to win it. With best play, mate comes in at most 33 moves from almost any position; a player who does not know the way goes round in circles, and the fifty-move rule hands the opponent a draw. The defending king runs to the wrong corner, and the three pieces must work together to drive it to the corner of the bishop's colour.

The Frenchman {{Philidor|francois-andre-philidor}} already dealt with this mate in the new edition, from 1777, of his famous 1749 book, and drew attention to a knight route now known as the W manoeuvre. The complete method, with the triangles you are about to learn, was published in 1923 by Daniel Delétang; some of its ideas date back to 1780.
practice: Now the real ending: king on e1, bishop on f1, knight on b1 and the black king on d5, in the centre. Barrier, Delétang's triangles and final net, within the fifty-move rule. Choose the pace and go.
part.finalNet.title: Final mating net
part.finalNet.summary: You coordinated the check with control of the escape squares. To build the mating net, relate the corner to the bishop and keep the pieces protected.
part.drive.title: The barrier
part.drive.summary: Together, the three pieces form a barrier that shrinks the black king's area to the edge, without losing a piece.
key.canto: With a light-squared bishop, mate can only be forced near a8 or h1, the corners of the bishop's colour. In a dark corner, the bishop never checks the cornered king.
key.barreira: To drive the black king to a8, the corner of the bishop's colour, the bishop closes the diagonal from a2 to g8. Here the black king can still cross on dark squares, such as d4: the knight goes to f5 and closes them. Then the king and the knight shrink the barrier to the edge.
key.triangulo: Delétang's triangles: the bishop on the diagonal from b1 to h7 traps the black king between it, the first rank and the h-file. With the passages closed by the king and the knight, the bishop moves to the smaller diagonal, and the triangle shrinks towards h1.
key.borda: With a dark-squared bishop, the black king on a8 is in the wrong corner. Delétang's triangles take it along the eighth rank to h8, and the whole game must fit within the fifty-move rule.
ex.finalNetAssessment01: Play White and deliver mate. The black king is trapped in the h8 corner.
ex.finalNetAssessment01.hint: The bishop can only check along a free diagonal. Open its path without releasing the black king; then the knight and bishop complete the mating net.
ex.finalNetAssessment01.solution: 1.Ne6 frees the bishop's diagonal and closes g7; the black king only has h7 left. After 1...Kh7, 2.Nf8+ forces 2...Kh8, because the bishop covers h6. Then 3.Bd4# mates along the long diagonal: the knight closes h7, and the king g7 and g8.
ex.finalNetAssessment01.r1: 1...Kh7. It is the black king's only square: your king covers g7 and g8.
ex.finalNetAssessment01.r2: 2...Kh8. The black king goes back to the corner, its only square: the bishop watches h6, and your king g6, g7 and g8.
part.deletang.title: Delétang's triangles
part.deletang.summary: From the wrong corner to the right one along the edge: the bishop closes a triangle and moves to the smaller parallel one, without opening an escape, until the mating net.
part.convert.title: From the centre to mate
part.convert.summary: The whole game: barrier, Delétang's triangles and final net, recognising the stage at every move and within the fifty-move rule.
ex.deletangAssessment01: Play White and find the best move. The bishop watches the diagonal from b1 to h7, and the black king is on h4, near the h1 corner.
ex.deletangAssessment01.hint: Your king on f6 already closes g5. Which piece can shrink the triangle now?
ex.deletangAssessment01.solution: 1.Bd1 moves the bishop to the diagonal from d1 to h5 and closes g4 and h5; with your king on f6 watching g5, the black king is in the middle triangle, with only g3 and h3. 1.Kf5 and 1.Nd3 also win, but leave the bishop on the diagonal from b1 to h7 and take five and three moves longer; the checks 1.Nf3+ and 1.Ng2+ take seven.
ex.deletangAssessment02: Play White and find the best move. The black king is on h1, in the small triangle, and has only h2.
ex.deletangAssessment02.hint: Before taking away the black king's last square, check that your move gives check.
ex.deletangAssessment02.solution: 1.Bg2+, with the bishop protected by your king: after 1...Kh2, 2.Ng4 is mate. 1.Bf1 and 1.Kg3 also win without stalemate, one move slower. 1.Nf3 and 1.Ng4 take h2 away without check: the black king has no move, it is stalemate, and a draw.
ex.driveAssessment01: Play White and find the best move. The bishop is light-squared, and the black king is on f4, still in the centre.
ex.driveAssessment01.hint: The bishop and the knight already cover some squares around the black king. Which piece closes the ones on the e-file?
ex.driveAssessment01.solution: 1.Kd4 closes e3, e4 and e5. With the bishop covering f5 and the knight g4, the barrier is closed: the black king only has f3, g3 and g5, away from the centre. 1.Kd5 also wins, but leaves e3 free and takes two moves longer.
ex.driveAssessment02: Play White and find the best move. The barrier is closed, and the black king is trapped near the a1 corner, the one of the bishop's colour.
ex.driveAssessment02.hint: No piece needs to advance. How can you pass the turn without opening any square?
ex.driveAssessment02.solution: 1.Bf2 is a waiting move: the bishop stays on the a7–g1 diagonal, with c5 and d4 closed, and the black king has to give ground. 1.Bg1, 1.Be3 and 1.Ba7 also wait on the diagonal; a knight move leaves d5 free, and on d4 the bishop is unprotected.
ex.convertAssessment01: Play White and find the three best moves. There have been 35 moves without a capture: under the fifty-move rule, mate must come within 15. The black king is on a5, near a8, the corner of the bishop's colour.
ex.convertAssessment01.hint: Recognise the stage: the black king is trapped on the a-file, near a8, the corner of the bishop's colour. Close one square at a time, without letting any go.
ex.convertAssessment01.solution: 1.Nb2 closes a4: the black king only has a6. After 1...Ka6, 2.Nc4 closes a5, and the black king only has a7. After 2...Ka7, 3.Kc6 closes b6 and b7: the black king is left between a6, a8 and b8, and the final net begins. After 3.Kc6, mate comes in six more moves, within the fifty-move rule.
ex.convertAssessment01.r1: 1...Ka6. It is the black king's only square: the knight closes a4, and your king b4, b5 and b6.
ex.convertAssessment01.r2: 2...Ka7. It is the only square: the knight closes a5, the bishop b7, and your king b5 and b6.
